title: Bilateral grip asymmetry does not improve frozen-model prediction of log albuminuria across two NHANES samples
abstract: We tested whether handgrip asymmetry adds predictive value beyond combined grip and renal/metabolic measures in adults aged 40–79. Models fitted in 2,425 NHANES 2011–12 participants were frozen and tested in 2,781 separately sampled 2013–14 participants. Adding a spline of absolute bilateral maximum-grip difference divided by their sum increased MEC-weighted mean squared error for natural-log urinary albumin/creatinine from 0.844480 to 0.848913. Gain (baseline minus augmented) was -0.004433, with a conditional-source 95% target-PSU bootstrap interval of [-0.007110, -0.001762]. Source out-of-fold results and all specified target sensitivity point estimates also favored omission. This negative feature-engineering result neither establishes biological absence of association nor evaluates persistent kidney disease or clinical utility.
